doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Studio work as a way to earn a living
summary: Ellis says studio work meant playing every style and instrument, and he enjoyed only the money.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: How is doing studio work different from playing live?

Well for me, and I think for most people that play studio work, it’s just a way of earning a living. You can play with a big orchestra maybe backing a vocalist and then you could be doing a rock session. And go from there to a country session. So you just have to play all styles. And being a guitarist you have to play every instrument. You have to play the guitar, the banjo, the ukulele, the mandolin.
